clue.text: Mostly useless runner failing to finish in twilight

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word for useless is dropped
something that fails to finish stops short, so the runner word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a dud is something useless
a ski is a runner on snow

explanation.surface: A hopeless athlete who never completes a race, still out there as the light fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is a ski, the runner a skier glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the dim period of fading light just after sunset, which is what twilight names.

clue.text: Factor is contributing to separation abandoned by church

indicators.note: being abandoned by something means it leaves, so the letters for church walk out of the word for separation
the little word is contributing to the inside of the other word, placed within it

blocks.note: a divorce is a marital separation
CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that helped bring about a split that the church refused to recognise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Factor' and 'separation' both sound like a breakup story; here they belong to arithmetic and marriage law, with the church abbreviation leaving before the little word goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A divisor is a number that divides another exactly, which mathematicians also call a factor.

clue.text: No ultimate sign of wear in this small travel iron?

definitions.text: No ultimate sign of wear in this

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a trip is a spell of travel
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a compact travel iron that seems to leave clothes unworn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like the household appliance; it is a golf club. The definition is cryptic: at the end of the act nothing is left on, so no last item of wear is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue where performers undress completely is a place where finally not one garment remains visible on stage.

clue.text: After delaying line, worth digesting Dickens play

indicators.note: delaying the line means the letter for line is moved later in the word, a rearrangement of its letters
digesting means swallowing something so it sits inside

blocks.note: value is another word for worth
as in 'what the dickens', where dickens is a euphemism for the devil

explanation.surface: Someone digesting a Dickens play after holding up a line, perhaps of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens' suggests the novelist, but it is the old euphemism in 'what the dickens'. Delaying the line means its letter moves one place later before the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaudeville is a light theatrical entertainment of songs and comic sketches, so a kind of stage play.

clue.text: Long distance runner, one in old women’s race

blocks.note: first meaning: a river runs, and this South American one runs for thousands of miles
second meaning: a member of the legendary tribe of warrior women in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A marathon runner taking part in an old ladies' race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' and 'race' both point at athletics, but the first is a river and the second a people.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South American river flows a vast distance, and in myth this was also the name for a warrior woman.

clue.text: Make out first of month by going around husband

indicators.note: one word going around another wraps it, holding the second inside

blocks.note: the first of December, written as Dec I in Roman numerals
per means by, as in 'per post'
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An instruction to fill in a document by the first of the month, with help from a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of month' looks like a request for an initial letter, but it is a date: Dec I, the first of December. PER then goes around H.
explanation.definitionFit: To decipher something is to work out its meaning, and to make out a message is to understand it.

clue.text: Frugal vicar not working 24/7, possibly

indicators.note: something not working is out of order, so these letters are out of their order too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thrifty clergyman who never takes time off, on duty around the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '24/7' reads as round-the-clock work, but here it is a number: twenty-four sevenths.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgar fraction is one written as numerator over denominator, and twenty-four over seven is an example.

clue.text: Thread through northern town missing vehicle

indicators.note: a town missing something lacks it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria, in the far north-west of England
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Following a thread across a northern town that is short of transport.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CAR from the start of CARLISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton yarn, originally made in the French city of Lille, used for stockings.

clue.text: Doctor pleased to have passed

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are tampered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician delighted that a patient got through an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person, but it is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has gone by, so it has passed, both past forms of verbs.

clue.text: Typical delegate

blocks.note: first meaning: characteristic of its kind, a fair example
second meaning: a person chosen to speak or act for others

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something serving as a fair sample and a noun for someone sent on behalf of others.

clue.text: Maybe Lynn pots mountain plant

indicators.note: to pot something is to put it into a container, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: Dame Vera Lynn was the British wartime singer, so Lynn is the surname of a Vera
ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A gardener called Lynn potting up an alpine plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pots' sounds like gardening, which fits the plant, but it is the container signal. Ben for mountain comes from Scottish peak names like Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a genus of flowering garden plants, also called vervain, with small clustered blooms.

clue.text: Back in flat, select instrument

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
back says to read the letters backwards, from right to left

blocks.note: the end of flat and most of select

explanation.surface: Choosing an instrument once you are home in your flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates, giving a bell-like sound.

clue.text: Proserpine, frantic with lust, beds a group containing Mars?

indicators.note: frantic means wild and disordered, so these letters are thrown into disorder
to bed something is to fix it inside, as plants are bedded in soil

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Roman goddess of the underworld, crazed with desire, seduces Mars, the god of war.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars reads as the war god, fitting the myth of Proserpine, but the definition wants the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers call the planets orbiting beyond Earth superior, and Mars is the nearest of them.

clue.text: Enjoy and let go, ignoring trendy question

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out of account, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: to relinquish is to let go
in means fashionable
QU is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: Advice to enjoy life and let go, without worrying about fashionable questions.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IN and QU out of the middle of RELINQUISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to take great pleasure in it, which is what enjoying means.

clue.text: Fragrant vapour having appeared intermittently outside

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so only every other letter is used
outside says one set of letters goes around the other

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
a fume is a vapour

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling mist that has drifted in now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfumed means scented with a pleasant smell, so fragrant is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drink raised pulse on a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: gram is a pulse, a legume such as chickpea or mung bean
taken as written
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A drink that sets a girl's pulse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' suggests a heartbeat; it is a bean.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a cocktail of tequila, lime juice and orange liqueur, often served in a salt-rimmed glass.

clue.text: Protectively coated adenoids malfunctioning

indicators.note: something malfunctioning is not in working order, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient whose adenoids have gone wrong and need a protective coating.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodised metal has had an oxide layer built up electrolytically to resist corrosion, a protective surface treatment.

clue.text: Football team, one welcoming new scorer

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so a letter is let inside

blocks.note: Albion is part of several English club names, such as West Bromwich Albion and Brighton and Hove Albion
I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A football club taking in a new goalscorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests a goalscorer, which suits the football team, but it means someone who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomaso Albinoni was a Venetian Baroque composer, and a composer writes scores, so a scorer.

clue.text: Loving Muslim Filipino embraced by two kinds of American

indicators.note: being embraced by something means being held within it

blocks.note: A is one abbreviation for American
the Moro are the Muslim peoples of the southern Philippines
US is a second abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A tender scene of a Filipino Muslim hugged by two Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: The two kinds of American are two abbreviations, A and US, which go either side of MORO.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means showing romantic or sexual desire, which is a loving disposition.

clue.text: Strict name indicator

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
an arrow is a pointer or indicator

explanation.definitionFit: Narrow can mean rigidly limited, as in a narrow interpretation, so strict in the sense of exact.

clue.text: The setter is cursed with old doctrine in Early English

definitions.note: a cry rather than a statement: the setter speaking of himself

indicators.note: in says the doctrine word sits inside the pair of letters that follow

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for early
an ism is a doctrine or ideology
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: The setter complains of being cursed with an outdated creed from early English history.
explanation.walkthrough: Early English sounds like a period of history or architecture, but it is two separate abbreviations that hold ISM between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is me is a lament someone says of their own misfortune, so a setter using it declares himself cursed.

clue.text: Minor example of House and The Observer initially supporting British PM once

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of each word is used
in a down clue whatever is supporting sits underneath, so those letters come after the British abbreviation

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a hut is a small, humble sort of house
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a minor house and the Observer backing a former British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the following letters underneath B. 'British PM once' tempts towards a former British prime minister, but British is only the B; Benazir and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto were prime ministers of Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Two members of the Bhutto family, father and daughter, each served as Pakistan's head of government in the past.

clue.text: Leave little room for airport customs inspection? That’s easily decided

definitions.text: Leave little room for airport customs inspection?
definitions.note: a cryptic hint at a suitcase opened and closed at once, rather than a synonym

blocks.clueFragment: Leave little room for airport customs inspection?
blocks.note: first meaning, cryptically: luggage that customs officers open and close again almost immediately
second meaning: a legal matter or question with an obvious outcome

explanation.surface: A traveller hurrying through customs with a bag that needs barely a glance.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads literally: a case, meaning a suitcase, opened and shut in no time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a matter, often legal, so clear-cut that its outcome is obvious without lengthy argument.

clue.text: Penetrate heart of USA, not getting caught

indicators.note: not getting something means going without it, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: center is the American spelling of centre, a heart
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of USA' looks like a request for the middle letter of USA; instead it asks for the American spelling of the word for heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter something is to go into it, which is the sense of penetrate.

clue.text: Dupes four unclothed idiots

indicators.note: unclothed means stripped of outer covering, so the word's outside letters go

blocks.note: the middle two letters
twits are idiots

explanation.surface: Four naked fools being taken in, a farce in one line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dupes' looks like a noun for victims, but it is the verb: tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone is to get the better of them by cunning, and to dupe someone is to trick them.

clue.text: Enormous belt snaps on 37.5 per cent of trousers

indicators.note: three-eighths of an eight-letter word is its first three letters

blocks.note: the opening three of its eight letters
snaps and pics are both informal words for photographs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' and 'trousers' make a wardrobe picture, but the belt is a band around the Earth and snaps are photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the wide zone circling Earth between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, a vast band.

clue.text: Criminal resorted to the obvious way out?

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook who simply walked out through the obvious exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun, the crook, but it is the adjective signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A street door is a building's main entrance opening on to the road, plainly the expected exit.

clue.text: Hack stone

blocks.note: first meaning: a worn-out old horse
second meaning: a green gemstone used for carvings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests cutting or a journalist; here it is a tired horse.
